summary: Carrie sits with the household as procedural guide rather than author, making clear that she can explain the process but cannot pre-write what any applicant will say.

panelPlan.action: Carrie is still standing with the notice while everyone else remains seated.
Bjorn slides the empty chair out with his boot. No one comments on the gesture.
Carrie looks at the chair, then at the partly unanswered review notice.
Carrie sits at the same level as everyone else.
Bjorn pushes the notice toward her, but not the answers.

dialogueInline.text: I can tell you what they are allowed to ask. I cannot write what you mean.

summary: Astrid returns from an ordinary independent day; Carrie stops herself from turning the arrival into an intake interview and asks only whether Astrid is willing to face the review herself.
settingText: Fifth-floor hallway and Safe Cave table, early evening.

panelPlan.action: Astrid comes up the stairs carrying a small reusable bag and one folded receipt or paper. Nothing about the props suggests a secret job or dramatic mission.
The door opens with Astrid's own key. Carrie looks up from the table and reflexively starts to ask where she has been.
Carrie catches herself mid-question and changes course.
Astrid sees the notice and the others around the table. Nobody briefs her before she sits.
Astrid puts the small bag down by her chair and answers only the question Carrie actually asked.

dialogueInline.text: Will you answer them for yourself tomorrow?

summary: Astrid refuses a rehearsal without being evasive: she knows what matters to her, but she does not offer the household or Carrie a preview of the life the hearing will later uncover.
settingText: Safe Cave table, continuing the council.

panelPlan.action: Carrie tests one obvious question, careful not to slip back into caseworker mode.
Astrid answers the immediate part without expanding into a speech.
Carrie waits for more. Astrid looks at the brass key and then at the closed door she entered through herself.
Bjorn almost follows up, then chooses not to. His silence is the behavioral beat.
Astrid keeps the small folded receipt or paper to herself and joins the table without explaining her day.

dialogueInline.text: Do you want to keep this home?
The rest they can ask me.

summary: The second male Kin worries that the hearing will demand certainty about a future he does not have; Bjorn no longer tries to supply that certainty for him.
settingText: Safe Cave window and table edge, later that evening.

panelPlan.action: Second Male Kin stands near the window holding the transit card, separated slightly from the table conversation.
Bjorn joins him without blocking the window or route back to the room.
He looks toward the city rather than toward the review notice.
Carrie answers only the procedural part.
Bjorn leaves the uncertainty with the man who owns it.

dialogueInline.text: Do not borrow an answer from me.
Say only what is yours when they ask.

summary: Carrie reduces preparation to the records actually required for entry into the hearing and explicitly refuses to turn private relationships or rehearsed narratives into advance evidence.
settingText: Safe Cave table, night; thin review file and printer pages.

panelPlan.action: Carrie narrows the materials to a thin stack: identity papers, residence records, required notices and the review letter. The symbolic household objects stay off the stack.
Carrie clips the required documents together.
Gunnar gestures toward a private support-group note that is not in the stack.
Silas holds the two clean printer pages from his bounded task, with his phone still in his pocket.
Carrie takes the printer pages, adds only what is required, and closes the file. Nobody practices testimony.

dialogueInline.text: IDs. Residence. Notices. What the hearing requires. Nothing else unless someone chooses it.
I made copies and no documentary.

summary: The household ends the night without a shared script. They know their wants differ and that tomorrow each person will have to answer for themselves.
settingText: Safe Cave, late night; table mostly cleared, brass key visible.

panelPlan.action: The table is mostly clear. Gunnar closes a book. The two male Kin separate into their evening routines. Astrid puts away her small bag. Carrie stands to leave.
The brass key remains near the closed hearing file. No written household statement sits beside it.
Carrie pauses with one hand on the doorframe.
Bjorn looks first at the closed file, then at the people around the room.
Nobody offers him a collective answer. He accepts that.
Carrie leaves. Bjorn picks up the brass key and closes the door on a household that is prepared to appear, not rehearsed to agree.

dialogueInline.text: Do you know what you're going to say?
